answer: Each identity seals a unique 32 GB replica of the network ledger by running a slow encoding keyed to its public key, which costs about 3 GPU-hours. Every epoch a beacon picks 20 random sectors and the agent must return Merkle openings within 2 seconds, so fetching from a shared copy fails. Each missed audit slashes a 40 token bond. Ten thousand clones need 320 TB of disk, roughly $4,800 in drives, plus 30,000 GPU-hours near $12,000, and one quill-signed audit thread per clone. Faking uniqueness is like hauling ten thousand basalt columns, each cut from its own quarry.
